headline: On November 19, 1999: Shenzhou 1 launched China's first spacecraft
captionCards: 14 orbits completed before reentry from Namibia
First step toward China’s crewed space missions
instagramCaption:
Shenzhou 1 blasted off on November 19, 1999.

China’s first uncrewed Shenzhou spacecraft launched atop a Long March 2F rocket. It completed 14 orbits before reentry, guided by the Yuan Wang 3 tracking ship off Namibia. The capsule landed safely in Inner Mongolia—415 km east of launch, 110 km northwest of Wuhai.

Its emergency escape system worked without a life-support system, proving key safety tech for future crewed missions.

This milestone laid the foundation for China’s human spaceflight program.
